title: Web search result, version 1
description: The result member of what the source web-search answers (docs/web-search.md): links to read, and for a grounded answer the text the provider generated, kept apart from them. A result is a lead and not a document. Each value is checked on its own, with patterns written to mean the same under a JavaScript and a Python regular-expression engine. The schema is looser than the adapter in these places, and a value it admits may be one the adapter never writes: a length is counted here in characters and by the adapter in bytes of UTF-8; a link is not parsed here, so one with user information or another port is admitted; that the hits are no more than the request's maxResults, and that no link is there twice, are rules that relate values and are the adapter's; that retrievedAt is a day of the calendar is not checked, only that its month, day, hour, minute and second are each within their range; a text is not held to the canonical domain of SPEC.md section 1.1, so one with half of a surrogate pair is admitted, which the adapter cannot write; and 1.0 is the integer 1 here.

revision.description: its revision when it was asked, and still when the answer was kept

query.description: the query of the request, as given

retrievedAt.description: when the answer had been read, to the second, in UTC

kind.description: search-results: links a search engine returned; grounded-answer: text a model generated, with the links it was grounded in

hits.description: the links, in the provider's order; at most the request's maxResults

generatedAnswer.description: what the model wrote, cut at 12000 bytes of UTF-8; generated text, not an excerpt of any page; absent where the model wrote none

attributionHtml.description: the provider's attribution markup, passed through as given: markup the adapter did not write and did not read, which a consumer renders as it would any markup from elsewhere

queries.description: the searches the provider says it made, each cut at 2000 bytes of UTF-8; absent where it names none

title.description: the provider's title for the link, cut at 512 bytes of UTF-8 and at a whole character; it may be empty, and it is the provider's text, which may hold any character

url.description: the provider's link as given, at most 4096 bytes; the adapter keeps a link only if it parses as an HTTPS URL that names a host, carries no user information and names no port or the port written 443; it need not be the address of the page it leads to

snippet.description: the provider's excerpt, cut at 2000 bytes of UTF-8 and at a whole character; the provider's text, not text read from the page; empty for a grounded answer, which has none
